root_cause.text: The function `contpte_ptep_set_access_flags` incorrectly uses the gathered `ptep_get()` value (which ORs AF/dirty from all sub-PTEs in the CONT range) to determine if the requested access flags are already set, causing false no-op detection when only a sibling sub-PTE has been updated but the target sub-PTE still has PTE_RDONLY or lacks PTE_AF, leading to infinite fault loops for page-table walkers that evaluate each descriptor individually.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "contpte_ptep_set_access_flags() compared the gathered ptep_get() value against the requested entry to detect no-ops. ptep_get() ORs AF/dirty from all sub-PTEs in the CONT block, so a dirty sibling can make the target appear already-dirty. When the gathered value matches entry, the function returns 0 even though the target sub-PTE still has PTE_RDONLY set in hardware." It further explains that this causes false no-ops for write faults (target still needs PTE_RDONLY cleared) and read faults (target still lacks PTE_AF). The patch introduces `contpte_all_subptes_match_access_flags` to check each sub-PTE individually using raw per-PTE values, thereby fixing the root cause.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a guard helper to check that all sub-PTEs in a contiguous block match the intended access flags before performing a set-access-flags operation, ensuring consistency and improving efficiency.
intent_record.what: Added a static helper function `contpte_all_subptes_match_access_flags` that, given a PTE pointer and an entry, checks whether all sub-PTEs in the contiguous block (aligned to CONT_PTES) have the same access-related flags (AF, DIRTY, write permission) as the supplied entry.
intent_record.how: The function iterates over the aligned contiguous PTE block, extracts a mask of PTE_RDONLY, PTE_AF, PTE_WRITE, PTE_DIRTY from each sub-PTE, and compares it to the masked entry; returns true only if all match. This enables callers (e.g., `contpte_ptep_set_access_flags`) to decide whether a full set of access flags is already consistent, avoiding unnecessary updates or TLB invalidations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix false no-op in contpte_ptep_set_access_flags by checking per-sub-PTE matching and using raw PTE value to avoid incorrect early return on hardware that evaluates descriptors individually.
intent_record.what: Replaced the early return check that used the gathered pte (via ptep_get) with a new helper contpte_all_subptes_match_access_flags that checks each sub-PTE individually. Changed the orig_pte assignment to use __ptep_get (raw per-PTE value) instead of ptep_get.
intent_record.how: Prevents false no-op returns when only a sibling PTE has been updated but the target sub-PTE still needs access/dirty bits set. Ensures that updates are performed when any sub-PTE in the CONT block does not match the requested flags, and uses the raw target PTE for subsequent write-bit unfolding decisions.
